_comment: Store profile: the routing taxonomy as DATA, not code.
Structure follows how dealerships actually organise: Fixed Operations (service, parts,
body shop) and Variable Operations (sales, F&I). Tires and detailing are SERVICE SUB-QUEUES,
not peer departments; roadside is a policy flag, not a place. A store with no body shop
deletes that destination; a store with its own tire centre promotes it to level 1 by moving
Edit this file per store. No code changes required.
name: Industry default dealership
_questions_note: The question text lives here, not in code, because the SAME string must be used when training
and at inference. The fine-tune learns to answer this exact instruction; if the training copy
drifts from the runtime copy the model is asked a question it was never trained on. Both read
these templates, so they cannot disagree.
`{label}` is substituted with the destination's label.

questions.destination: Which part of the dealership should handle this caller? Pick where the work belongs, not the first thing the caller mentioned.
questions.subqueue: This is a {label} call. What exactly does the caller want, and which sub-queue should it go to? Pick the single closest option.

_unsafe_threshold_note: 0.3, not 0.5, and that is a measured choice rather than a round number. On the 45-case
severity set, lowering dispatch from 0.5 to 0.3 raises recall of unsafe callers from 0.778
to 0.833 while precision stays at 1.000 - it catches one more stranded caller and sends no
extra trucks. The errors are asymmetric: a missed stranded caller is someone at the side of
a road, a false alarm is a wasted journey. Recall leads, so the bar sits low.

_facts_note: What the switchboard can ANSWER rather than route. Measured: hours and directions is one of
the top repeatable Fixed Ops call types, so answering it is real call volume, not a nicety.
A store edits these; the agent reads them instead of transferring a factual question.

facts.name: Riverside Motors
facts.hours: Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm, Saturday 8am to 4pm, closed Sunday
facts.loaner_policy: A loaner car is available on request for any service taking longer than a day
facts.directions: From the highway take exit 12 and follow Riverside Drive for half a mile

_schedule_note: `minutes` is how long the BOOKED SLOT occupies, not how long the repair takes. A collision
repair takes days but the appointment is a drop-off and assessment, so its slot is an hour.
That distinction is what makes a slot offer fit inside a working day; a 1440-minute 'slot'
could never be offered at all.
`bays` is how many jobs of that type can run at once.
Sub-queues absent from `services` fall back to `default`; `no_appointment` marks work that is

collision.note: drop-off and assessment; the repair takes days
